sn45.34:3.1: These verses also occur in the context of the seven awakening factors (SN 46.17:2.1), the tenfold path (AN 10.117:2.1, AN 10.118:3.1), the ten ways of skillful deeds (AN 10.169:3.1, AN 10.170:2.1), and as independent verses (Dhp 85–89).
sn45.34:5.1: While the text has the singular dhamma here, the commentary explains it by way of the contrast between “dark” qualities and “bright” qualities, which are typically in plural. And indeed, the Sanskrit parallels of this verse have the plural form. See Norman’s note on Dhp 87 in his The Word of the Doctrine.
sn45.34:5.2: Bhāvetha here is a rare reflexive form for the third person optative singular, agreeing with pariyodapeyya below.
sn45.34:5.3: The Pali for “home” is oka, which I elsewhere disambiguate by rendering as “bastion”.
sn45.34:7.2: For “awakening factors” the Pali has sambodhiyaṅga, which is a different spelling of sambojjhaṅga, familiar from the “seven awakening factors”.
